items.stem: Which is NOT a cause of depreciation?
options: An increase in the market value of the asset
items.answer: An increase in the market value of the asset
items.markingKey: An increase in the market value of the asset. Depreciation reflects consumption of the asset [1]

items.stem: Explain why non-current assets are depreciated.
items.answer: Their cost is spread over the years that benefit from their use (matching concept), so profit in each year bears a fair share and the carrying amount reflects consumption of the asset.
items.markingKey: Spread cost over useful life [1]; matching/fair profit [1] [2]

items.stem: State two causes of depreciation.
items.answer: Wear and tear; obsolescence; passage of time (e.g. a lease); depletion (e.g. a mine).
items.markingKey: Any two [1 each] [2]

items.stem: Savanna Tours bought a printing press for $57,200 on 1 January 2024. It is expected to have a useful life of 4 years and a residual value of $4,000. Depreciation is charged using the straight-line method. The financial year ends on 31 December. Calculate the annual depreciation charge.

Harbour Electrics bought a refrigeration unit for $58,900 on 1 July 2024. It is expected to have a useful life of 4 years and a residual value of $4,500. Depreciation is charged using the straight-line method on a monthly basis (time apportioned). The financial year ends on 31 December. (a) Calculate the annual depreciation charge. (b) Calculate the depreciation for the year ended 31 December 2024.

Baobab Furnishings bought a coffee roaster for $22,500 on 1 July 2024. It is expected to have a useful life of 10 years and a residual value of $4,500. Depreciation is charged using the straight-line method on a monthly basis (time apportioned). The financial year ends on 31 December. (a) Calculate the annual depreciation charge. (b) Calculate the carrying amount of the asset at 31 December 2025.

Cedar Hardware bought a machine for $35,500 on 1 September 2024. It is expected to have a useful life of 10 years and a residual value of $4,500. Depreciation is charged using the straight-line method on a monthly basis (time apportioned). The financial year ends on 31 December. (a) Calculate the annual depreciation charge. (b) Calculate the depreciation for the year ended 31 December 2024.

Savanna Tours bought a computer system for $45,500 on 1 April 2024. It is expected to have a useful life of 10 years and a residual value of $2,500. Depreciation is charged using the straight-line method on a monthly basis (time apportioned). The financial year ends on 31 December. (a) Calculate the annual depreciation charge. (b) Calculate the depreciation for the year ended 31 December 2024. (c) Explain why the carrying amount of the computer system is unlikely to equal its market value.
items.answer: (a) $4,300 (b) $3,225 (c) Depreciation allocates cost over useful life using estimates; it does not try to measure the asset's current market value.

items.stem: Explain why depreciation is a non-cash expense.
items.answer: It allocates cost already paid when the asset was bought; no cash leaves the business when depreciation is charged.
items.markingKey: Allocation of past cost [1]; no cash outflow [1] [2]

items.stem: Atlas Engineering bought a forklift truck for $15,500 on 1 May 2024. It is expected to have a useful life of 5 years and a residual value of $5,500. Depreciation is charged using the straight-line method on a monthly basis (time apportioned). The financial year ends on 31 December. (a) Calculate the annual depreciation charge. (b) Calculate the depreciation for the year ended 31 December 2024. (c) Calculate the carrying amount of the asset at 31 December 2025.
Complete the statement: Under the reducing-balance method, the depreciation charge …
options: is based on the original cost each year
items.answer: falls each year
items.markingKey: falls each year. A fixed % of a falling carrying amount [1]

items.stem: Explain one advantage of the reducing-balance method over the straight-line method.
items.answer: Higher charges in early years when the asset loses most value; total cost (depreciation + repairs) is more even over the asset's life.
items.markingKey: Early high charge matches value loss [1]; evens out depreciation + repairs [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain how the revaluation method of depreciation works.
items.answer: The items are valued at the end of each year; depreciation = opening value + purchases − closing valuation (less any disposal proceeds).
items.markingKey: Valued each year [1]; formula [1] [2]

items.stem: Volcano Spices bought a forklift truck for $17,000 at the start of year 1. It is depreciated at 20% per annum using the reducing-balance method. Calculate the depreciation charge for each of years 1 to 2.

Zambezi Timber bought a refrigeration unit for $22,000 at the start of year 1. It is depreciated at 30% per annum using the reducing-balance method. Calculate the depreciation charge for each of years 1 to 3.

Harbour Electrics uses the revaluation method for its loose tools. At 1 January they were valued at $2,780. During the year tools costing $1,080 were bought. At 31 December the tools were valued at $3,030. (a) Calculate the depreciation of loose tools for the year. (b) Explain why the revaluation method is suitable for loose tools.
items.answer: (a) $830 (b) They are numerous, low-value items with different lives; recording each separately would be impractical.
items.markingKey: (a) $2,780 + $1,080 − $3,030 = $830 [2] (b) Many small items [1]; impractical to depreciate individually [1] [2]

items.stem: Pacific Tiles uses the revaluation method for its loose tools. At 1 January they were valued at $3,990. During the year tools costing $2,300 were bought. At 31 December the tools were valued at $5,290. The bookkeeper calculated depreciation as −$1,300. Explain why this is wrong and determine the correct depreciation.
items.answer: The tools bought during the year were ignored. Correct depreciation: $1,000.
items.markingKey: Error explained: the tools bought during the year were ignored [1]; working: $3,990 + $2,300 − $5,290 [1]; correct depreciation: $1,000 [1] [3]

items.stem: Cedar Hardware uses the revaluation method for its loose tools. At 1 January they were valued at $2,690. During the year tools costing $1,580 were bought. At 31 December the tools were valued at $2,950. (a) Calculate the depreciation of loose tools for the year. (b) Explain why the revaluation method is suitable for loose tools.
items.answer: (a) $1,320 (b) They are numerous, low-value items with different lives; recording each separately would be impractical.
items.markingKey: (a) $2,690 + $1,580 − $2,950 = $1,320 [2] (b) Many small items [1]; impractical to depreciate individually [1] [2]

items.stem: Complete the statement: The annual depreciation charge is recorded by …
options: debiting bank and crediting the asset
debiting provision for depreciation and crediting bank
debiting the asset account and crediting depreciation
debiting depreciation (income statement) and crediting provision for depreciation
items.answer: debiting depreciation (income statement) and crediting provision for depreciation
items.markingKey: debiting depreciation (income statement) and crediting provision for depreciation. The asset stays at cost [1]

items.stem: Explain why depreciation is credited to a provision account rather than to the asset account.
items.answer: The asset account then shows the original cost while the provision shows accumulated depreciation; both are needed for the statement of financial position and for calculating disposals.
items.markingKey: Cost retained [1]; accumulated depreciation visible/disposals [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why accumulated depreciation is not a fund of cash.
items.answer: It is a book entry allocating cost; no money is set aside, so it cannot be used to buy replacement assets.
items.markingKey: Book entry only [1]; no cash set aside [1] [2]

items.stem: Pampas Leather bought equipment for $26,000 on 1 March 2024 and further equipment for $23,000 on 1 August 2025. Depreciation is charged at 10% per annum, straight-line on cost, with a full year's depreciation in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. The year end is 31 December. Calculate the depreciation charge for each of the years 2024, 2025 and 2026.

Baobab Furnishings bought equipment for $19,000 on 1 March 2024 and further equipment for $20,000 on 1 August 2025. Depreciation is charged at 20% per annum, straight-line on cost, with a full year's depreciation in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. The year end is 31 December. Calculate the depreciation charge for each of the years 2024, 2025 and 2026.

Cedar Hardware bought equipment for $14,000 on 1 March 2024 and further equipment for $30,000 on 1 August 2025. Depreciation is charged at 25% per annum, reducing balance, with a full year's depreciation in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. The year end is 31 December. (a) Calculate the depreciation charge for each of the years 2024, 2025 and 2026. (b) Calculate the carrying amount of the equipment at 31 December 2026.

Pacific Tiles bought equipment for $46,000 on 1 March 2024. Depreciation is charged at 20% per annum, straight-line on cost, with a full year's depreciation in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. The year end is 31 December. What is the balance on the provision for depreciation account at 31 December 2026?
Complete the statement: On disposal, the cost of the asset is transferred by …
options: debiting bank and crediting the asset
debiting the disposal account and crediting the asset account
debiting the asset account and crediting disposal
items.answer: debiting the disposal account and crediting the asset account
items.markingKey: debiting the disposal account and crediting the asset account. Remove the asset at cost [1]

items.stem: Explain why a profit on disposal does not necessarily mean the asset was a good investment.
items.answer: It only shows that the depreciation charged was more than the actual fall in value; it adjusts past estimates rather than measuring the asset's return.
items.markingKey: Adjustment of past depreciation estimates [1]; not a measure of return [1] [2]

items.stem: State the entries in the disposal account when an asset is sold for cash.
items.answer: Dr disposal with cost (Cr asset); Cr disposal with accumulated depreciation (Dr provision); Cr disposal with proceeds (Dr bank); balance = profit or loss to IS.
items.markingKey: Cost [1]; depreciation and proceeds [1] [2]

Depreciation was charged at 10% per annum straight-line on cost, a full year in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. After 2 full years the refrigeration unit was sold for $21,850 by bank transfer. Calculate the accumulated depreciation at the date of disposal.

Jade Ceramics bought a machine for $43,000. Depreciation was charged at 20% per annum straight-line on cost, a full year in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. After 3 full years the machine was given in part-exchange for a new machine costing $46,000; the supplier allowed $16,300 for the old one. Calculate the accumulated depreciation at the date of disposal.

Aurora Printing bought a coffee roaster for $32,000. Depreciation was charged at 25% per annum straight-line on cost, a full year in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. After 4 full years the coffee roaster was sold for $50 by bank transfer. (a) Calculate the accumulated depreciation at the date of disposal. (b) Calculate the profit or loss on disposal.

Atlas Engineering bought a machine for $28,000. Depreciation was charged at 25% per annum straight-line on cost, a full year in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. After 3 full years the machine was given in part-exchange for a new machine costing $35,000; the supplier allowed $8,550 for the old one. (a) Calculate the accumulated depreciation at the date of disposal. (b) Discuss whether Atlas Engineering should replace the machine now or keep it for longer.
items.answer: (a) $21,000 (b) Replacement brings efficiency and lower repairs but costs cash and may need finance; keeping it saves cash but repair costs and breakdown risk rise.
items.markingKey: (a) $7,000 + $7,000 + $7,000 = $21,000 [2] (b) Benefit of replacement [1]; cost/finance [1]; judgement [1] [3]

items.stem: Nile Valley Dairy bought a printing press for $13,000. (b) Discuss whether Nile Valley Dairy should replace the printing press now or keep it for longer.
items.answer: (a) $7,800 (b) Replacement brings efficiency and lower repairs but costs cash and may need finance; keeping it saves cash but repair costs and breakdown risk rise.
items.markingKey: (a) $2,600 + $2,600 + $2,600 = $7,800 [2] (b) Benefit of replacement [1]; cost/finance [1]; judgement [1] [3]

items.stem: Pampas Leather bought a printing press for $28,000. Depreciation was charged at 10% per annum straight-line on cost, a full year in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. After 2 full years the printing press was sold for $19,650 by bank transfer. A student calculated a loss on disposal of $8,350. State the mistake made and give the correct profit or loss on disposal.
items.answer: The proceeds were compared with the original cost; they must be compared with the carrying amount (cost less accumulated depreciation). Correct profit or loss on disposal: loss $2,750.
items.markingKey: Error: the proceeds were compared with the original cost; they must be compared with the carrying amount (cost less accumulated depreciation) [1]; correct profit or loss on disposal: loss $2,750 [1] [2]

items.stem: Volcano Spices bought a forklift truck for $54,000. Depreciation was charged at 10% per annum straight-line on cost, a full year in the year of purchase and none in the year of disposal. After 2 full years the forklift truck was sold for $39,500 by bank transfer. Calculate the accumulated depreciation at the date of disposal.
Under IAS 16, which cost should be included in the cost of a new machine?
options: Staff training on the new machine
Advertising the products it will make
items.answer: Installation and testing costs
items.markingKey: Installation and testing costs. Costs to bring the asset to working condition [1]

items.stem: Complete the statement: A non-current asset register records …
options: details of each asset such as cost, date of purchase, location, depreciation and carrying amount
the inventory held in the warehouse
items.answer: details of each asset such as cost, date of purchase, location, depreciation and carrying amount
items.markingKey: details of each asset such as cost, date of purchase, location, depreciation and carrying amount. Control over assets [1]

items.stem: Explain two benefits to a business of keeping a non-current asset register.
items.answer: Physical checks can detect theft or loss; depreciation and disposal calculations are easier; insurance and maintenance can be planned; the register can be reconciled with the ledger.
items.markingKey: Any two benefits [1 each] [2]

items.stem: Jade Ceramics bought a new refrigeration unit with a list price of $20,000, less 10% trade discount. The following were also paid: delivery $1,100, a one-year maintenance contract $2,200, testing $950. Calculate the cost of the refrigeration unit to be capitalised under IAS 16.
items.markingKey: $20,000 × 90% = $18,000 [1]; add delivery, testing [1]; exclude a one-year maintenance contract [1]; = $20,050 [1] [4]

items.stem: Atlas Engineering bought a new refrigeration unit with a list price of $77,000. The following were also paid: delivery $950, training of operators $550, testing $700, a one-year maintenance contract $1,050. (a) Calculate the cost of the refrigeration unit to be capitalised under IAS 16. (b) Explain how the asset register could help Atlas Engineering control its non-current assets.
items.answer: (a) $78,650 (b) Regular physical checks against the register reveal missing or idle assets; responsibility can be assigned by location.
items.markingKey: (a) add delivery, testing [1]; exclude training of operators, a one-year maintenance contract [1]; = $78,650 [1] [3] (b) Physical check [1]; control/responsibility [1] [2]

items.stem: Complete the statement: A machine costs $24,000, has a residual value of $4,000 and a useful life of 5 years. Straight-line depreciation per year is …

Depreciation is charged using the straight-line method on a monthly basis (time apportioned). The financial year ends on 31 December. An accounts assistant calculated annual depreciation as $9,750. Explain why this is wrong and determine the correct annual depreciation.
items.answer: The residual value was not deducted from cost before dividing by the useful life. Correct annual depreciation: $9,500.
items.markingKey: Error explained: the residual value was not deducted from cost before dividing by the useful life [1]; working: ($39,000 − $1,000) ÷ 4 [1]; correct annual depreciation: $9,500 [1] [3]

items.answer: They do not bring the asset itself to working condition; the benefit belongs to the staff, who may leave, so the cost is an expense (IAS 16).
